name: Puneshwar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple that stood on the bank of the Mutha river and from which the city of Pune takes its name; it was pulled down in the late 13th century and a dargah rose over the site, where temple artefacts resurfaced after a river wall collapsed in 2006.

name: Punjai Siva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Kaveri delta village of Punjai, about 6 km from Semponnarkoil, whose best-known possession is a bronze Nataraja cast around 1000 CE in the time of Rajendra Chola.

name: Pisharikavu Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali shrine built in the traditional Kerala manner at Kollam near Koyilandy, counted among the thirteen principal Shakteya temples of Kerala.

name: Perunna Subrahmanya Swami Temple
significance: A Kartikeya temple at Perunna in Changanassery, notable as the first temple in Kerala opened to Hindus of every caste, ahead of the state's own proclamation; Gandhi worshipped here during his first visit to Kerala.
story: The deity is said to stand in a furious mood immediately after slaying the asura Tarakasura, his vel pointing downward.

name: Prasanna Venkatachalapathi Temple, Thuraiyur
significance: A hilltop Vishnu temple on Perumalmalai about 3 km from Thuraiyur; it is traditionally held to have been founded by descendants of the early Chola king Karikala, who are themselves venerated at the shrine.

name: Pisharnath Mahadev Mandir
significance: The oldest temple in the hill station of Matheran, standing on the bank of Charlotte Lake, where Pisharnath is worshipped as the village deity in a swayambhu lingam of unusual L shape.

name: Punnainallur Mariamman Temple
significance: A Mariamman temple some 5 km east of Thanjavur whose small original shrine was raised in the reign of Tulaja and greatly enlarged by Serfoji II, who added the mahamandapa, narthana mandapa, gopura and second inner prakara; the Thanjavur court endowed it richly and connected it to the palace by an underground passage.
story: Legend holds that the sage Sadashiva Brahmendra formed the goddess's image from an anthill, and that the king founded the shrine after Mariamman appeared to him in a dream among the punnai trees that name the village.

name: Lakhesvara Siva Temple
significance: A 13th-century Shiva shrine on a saptaratha rekha-deula plan behind the Lingaraja market in Bhubaneswar's old town, a short distance northeast of the Lingaraja temple, enshrining a lingam set in a circular yonipitha; local tradition ascribes it to the Ganga rulers.

name: Sree Perunthatta Siva Temple
significance: A Kerala-style Shiva temple at Guruvayur with a double-storeyed tile-roofed sanctum; it lay under the Zamorin of Calicut and was wrecked during Tipu Sultan's 18th-century campaign, and excavation at the site has recovered two cannons from the defence mounted by the Zamorin's forces.
story: Folklore holds that the sage Parashurama installed the Shiva idol here in the Treta Yuga.

name: Venkatachalapathy Temple, Thiruvananthapuram
significance: A Vishnu temple a minute's walk from the southern gate of the Padmanabhaswamy temple in Thiruvananthapuram, built in 1898, its idol consecrated by the fortieth Azhagiya Singar of the Ahobila Matha; the sanctum follows Tamil rather than Kerala practice, without the elaborate carving or a gopuram.
story: The image is said to have been found in a pond near the house of Ranga Iyengar of Veeravanallur about a century before the temple was raised, and his family's eldest son has served as chief priest for three generations.

name: Shri Guru Kottureshwara Temple
significance: A Veerashaiva pilgrimage centre in the town of Kotturu, which takes its name from the saint Guru Kottureshwara; the complex is made up of four mathas, among them the Murkal Matha, where the saint is said to have first appeared, and the Darbar Matha, where he heard people's troubles.
story: Local tradition holds that Nandi came down from Kailasa in the form of the saint to protect the Veerashaiva faith, that those who harassed him were struck blind, and that he brought a dead buffalo back to life with a touch of his hand.

name: Kanichukulangara Devi Temple
significance: A Bhagavathi temple about 7.5 km from Cherthala in Alappuzha district, known for its Thiruvonam festival in the Malayalam month of Kumbham, with chikkara, pongala, thooka chadu and fireworks.

name: Sri Pralayakala Veerabadrar Temple
significance: A temple in the Gavipuram Guddadahalli neighbourhood of Bengaluru dedicated to Pralayakala Veerabadra.

name: Bagheswari Temple, Bongaigaon
significance: A goddess temple in the southern part of Bongaigaon city, described as one of the oldest of the fifty-one Shakti Pithas and a major Hindu pilgrimage stop in western Assam; its precinct preserves a medieval rock-cut Ganesha and architectural members of a stone temple datable to the 10th-11th century.

name: Siddheshwari Kali Mandir
significance: A Shakta temple in north-eastern Kalna near the Bhagirathi-Hooghly, built in 1740 by Chitrasen Roy, a zamindar of Burdwan, and regarded as a fine example of jor-bangla architecture; five 18th-century Shiva temples stand in the same compound and the image of the goddess, about five feet tall, is carved from neem wood.

name: Parasuramesvara Temple, Gudimallam
builtDisplay: later Chola-Vijayanagara structure; linga c. 2nd-1st c. BCE
significance: The temple at Gudimallam, about 24 km south-east of Tirupati, enshrines a linga that scholars count among the earliest surviving and unmistakable images of Shiva, dated variously from the 3rd-1st century BCE to the early centuries CE; the apsidal stone sanctuary around it is usually assigned to the later Chola and Vijayanagara periods, and the shrine, still in worship, has been protected by the Archaeological Survey of India since 1954.

name: Keleswaram Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Keleswaram in Thiruvananthapuram district, administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board, whose lingam faces west - an orientation the article notes as rare; Maha Shivaratri and Thiruvathira are its principal festivals.

name: Varahaperumal Temple, Kumbakonam
significance: A Vishnu temple in Kumbakonam where the god is worshipped in his boar incarnation alongside Bhoomidevi; it is one of the five Vishnu temples tied to the Mahamaham festival held there once every twelve years.
story: The temple recalls how a demon carried the earth down into the netherworld, and Vishnu took the form of a boar, fought him and raised the earth back up at the gods' plea.

name: Shri Dev Rameshwar Temple
place: Rameshwar Wadi, Devgad taluka, Sindhudurg district
significance: A 16th-century Shiva temple in Devgad taluka approached by a rock-cut passage some 250 yards long and fifty feet deep; the Angre admirals of the Maratha navy enlarged it through the 18th century and a sabha mandap was added in 1780, while its four-armed image seated on a bull is of solid silver said to weigh about a hundred kilograms and a bell taken from a captured Portuguese ship in 1791 hangs at the eastern gate.
